caption: Fig. 1: Main block diagram of the 2 × 2 mesh NoC. CPU, memory and AI names identify traffic-model endpoints; they are not implemented processors.
Fig. 2: Input FIFO heads, routing requests, per-output retained grants and crossbar selection.
Fig. 3: Active corner ports and boundary masks; logical port indices remain uniform.
Fig. 4: Bit allocation used by the shared VHDL packet package and dashboard decoder.
Fig. 5: XY routing for a valid FIFO head. Matching A circles join the five route branches to the output-request stage. X is resolved before Y.
Fig. 6: Retained grant through a stall and rotation after successful acceptance.
Fig. 7: Actual CSV-derived pre-edge state for a held grant; omitted stalled cycles are labelled.
Fig. 8: Synthesizable hierarchy and separation of core, finite demo endpoints and testbench.
Fig. 9: Vivado elaborated RTL schematic of the four-router core. The green wires show logical signal connections before technology mapping.
Fig. 10: Routed Local-output arbiter schematic, Screenshot 30. The selected view contains 32 cells and 89 nets, including LUTs and flip-flops.
Fig. 11: Accepted-event scoreboard: offer is not acceptance, and reset discards are explicit.

Fig. 12: Cropped original Screenshot 10: XSim tb_noc_2x2 receiver word and valid/ready before the 45 ns delivery edge. The yellow value cursor is 40 ns; the blue marker is 44.999 ns. Complete image: screenshot record, Step 10.
Fig. 13: All-to-all arithmetic means across three seeds; whiskers show observed minimum/maximum, not confidence intervals.
Fig. 14: Deterministic sustained-hotspot depth comparison with the same registered output controller.
Fig. 15: Refined dashboard using the actual directed-d4 trace at edge 231. Six link accepts and four stall events are recorded; R01 Local input is full.
Fig. 16: Cropped original Screenshot 16: later GUI noc_2x2_core synthesis hierarchy, xc7s15cpga196-2, DEPTH=4. The core and router totals are visible. Complete image: screenshot record, Step 16.

Fig. 17: Cropped original Screenshot 27: routed demo timing summary in Vivado 2026.1. Setup/hold margins are positive and TNS/THS are zero. External board timing remains unverified. Complete image: screenshot record, Step 27.

Fig. 18: Original Screenshot 25: four-router placement in the routed demonstration checkpoint. Colors identify selected router logic and show where the synthesized cells were placed in the FPGA fabric.
